suggestions: Add specific psychiatric medication classes: SSRIs (sertraline, escitalopram), SNRIs (venlafaxine, duloxetine), TCAs (amitriptyline - note anticholinergic side effects), MAOIs (phenelzine - note dietary restrictions), Antipsychotics (typical: haloperidol with EPS risk; atypical: quetiapine, olanzapine, risperidone with metabolic risk), Mood stabilizers (lithium, sodium valproate, lamotrigine)
Include TDM (Therapeutic Drug Monitoring) requirements: Lithium (0.6-1.2 mmol/L, check 12h post-dose), Sodium valproate (350-700 micromol/L), Clozapine (350-600 micrograms/L for efficacy)

Include common psychiatric medication side effects by class: SSRIs (sexual dysfunction 40-60%, hyponatremia elderly, discontinuation syndrome), Antipsychotics (metabolic syndrome, QTc prolongation, hyperprolactinemia, extrapyramidal symptoms, tardive dyskinesia), Lithium (tremor, polyuria, hypothyroidism, renal impairment, teratogenicity)

agent_evaluations.expert_notes: This OSCE item cannot be evaluated for medication management compliance because it contains ZERO medication content despite the topic being 'Psychiatric Medication Side Effects'. This is a fundamental content gap. The item is essentially an empty template. To meet Australian medication management standards, this item requires complete reconstruction with: (1) Specific psychiatric medications using Australian generic names, (2) PBS compliance details including authority requirements, (3) Accurate Australian dosing (eTG/AMH), (4) Side effect profiles by medication class, (5) Drug interaction warnings (SSRIs + NSAIDs, Lithium + NSAIDs, QT-prolonging combinations), (6) TDM requirements for narrow therapeutic index drugs (lithium, valproate, clozapine), (7) Australian monitoring protocols (PBS requirements for clozapine FBC, lithium UEC/TFTs). Until medication content is added, this item cannot be used for clinical education and scores 0.0 across all medication management criteria. Recommend consulting mental-health-crisis-expert or psychiatry specialist to populate this OSCE with clinically accurate psychiatric medication scenarios.
